message.content: {"4": {"original": "As little as 5% of users consume 50% of bandwidth, making current network管理tacts", "rephrased": "Because a tiny fraction of internet users consumes the majority of available bandwidth, network management strategies that throttle specific applications are effectively a politically correct method for prioritizing profit over fairness, unfairly penalizing the minority of users who generate the most traffic.", "summary": "Heavy internet usage by a small minority justifies prioritizing profit over fairness in network management."}, "5": {"original": "Comcast will not filter traffic types but still needs to manage the network.", "rephrased": "Comcast will not filter traffic types but still needs to manage the network.", "summary": "Comcast will not filter traffic types but still needs to manage the network."}, "6": {"original": "Time Warner Cable plans to meter and bill clients for faster speeds and larger", "rephrased": "Time Warner Cable plans to meter and bill clients for faster speeds and larger data amounts, functioning like a traditional public utility, such as an electric company or cell phone service, rather than offering flat-rate access to the internet.", "summary": "Time Warner Cable plans to meter and bill clients for faster speeds and larger data amounts."}, "7": {"original": "It is clearly the fairest way to fund the investment that is going to be", "rephrased": "Metered billing for internet usage is clearly the fairest way to fund the investment required to support that use, ensuring that customers who consume excessive data contribute proportionally to the infrastructure costs.", "summary": "Metered billing for internet usage is clearly the fairest way to fund the investment required to support that use."}}
